body:
You will select and use grammar from context while working with extra-curricular activities, school competitions, national celebrations.

science club: Use clues about science club to select and use grammar from context.; school tournament: Use clues about school tournament to select and use grammar from context.; Republic Day ceremony: Use clues about Republic Day ceremony to select and use grammar from context.; music rehearsal: Use clues about music rehearsal to select and use grammar from context.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a science club task, identify the clue first and then select and use grammar from context.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I select and use grammar from context? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

Outcome ENG.7.1.G1 develops the ability to select and use grammar from context through extra-curricular activities, school competitions, national celebrations.

The note supplies all language evidence in text. No decorative visual is used; any visual clue required by a future listening or reading stimulus must be bound to that stimulus.

group project: Use clues about group project to reflect on and share listening experiences.; revision timetable: Use clues about revision timetable to reflect on and share listening experiences.; class presentation: Use clues about class presentation to reflect on and share listening experiences.; library research: Use clues about library research to reflect on and share listening experiences.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a group project task, identify the clue first and then reflect on and share listening experiences.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I reflect on and share listening experiences? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

Outcome ENG.7.2.L4 develops the ability to reflect on and share listening experiences through classroom routines, learning strategies, study habits.

The note supplies all language evidence in text. No decorative visual is used; any visual clue required by a future listening or reading stimulus must be bound to that stimulus.

group project: Use clues about group project to prepare and plan before writing.; revision timetable: Use clues about revision timetable to prepare and plan before writing.; class presentation: Use clues about class presentation to prepare and plan before writing.; library research: Use clues about library research to prepare and plan before writing.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a group project task, identify the clue first and then prepare and plan before writing.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I prepare and plan before writing? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

Outcome ENG.7.2.W1 develops the ability to prepare and plan before writing through classroom routines, learning strategies, study habits.

The note supplies all language evidence in text. No decorative visual is used; any visual clue required by a future listening or reading stimulus must be bound to that stimulus.

body:
You will select and use grammar from context while working with daily routines, health, feelings and personal growth.

healthy breakfast: Use clues about healthy breakfast to select and use grammar from context.; sleep routine: Use clues about sleep routine to select and use grammar from context.; emotion journal: Use clues about emotion journal to select and use grammar from context.; weekend exercise: Use clues about weekend exercise to select and use grammar from context.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a healthy breakfast task, identify the clue first and then select and use grammar from context.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I select and use grammar from context? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

Outcome ENG.7.3.G1 develops the ability to select and use grammar from context through daily routines, health, feelings and personal growth.

body:
You will draft a clear written text while working with daily routines, health, feelings and personal growth.

healthy breakfast: Use clues about healthy breakfast to draft a clear written text.; sleep routine: Use clues about sleep routine to draft a clear written text.; emotion journal: Use clues about emotion journal to draft a clear written text.; weekend exercise: Use clues about weekend exercise to draft a clear written text.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a healthy breakfast task, identify the clue first and then draft a clear written text.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I draft a clear written text? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

body:
You will draft a clear written text while working with animals, habitats, weather and environmental responsibility.

forest habitat: Use clues about forest habitat to draft a clear written text.; weather forecast: Use clues about weather forecast to draft a clear written text.; recycling project: Use clues about recycling project to draft a clear written text.; wildlife observation: Use clues about wildlife observation to draft a clear written text.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a forest habitat task, identify the clue first and then draft a clear written text.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I draft a clear written text? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

Outcome ENG.7.7.W3 develops the ability to draft a clear written text through animals, habitats, weather and environmental responsibility.

The note supplies all language evidence in text. No decorative visual is used; any visual clue required by a future listening or reading stimulus must be bound to that stimulus.

body:
You will use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing while working with space, technology, future plans and imagination.

space mission: Use clues about space mission to use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing.; future classroom: Use clues about future classroom to use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing.; robot assistant: Use clues about robot assistant to use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing.; planet research: Use clues about planet research to use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing.

Use English clues, familiar experiences and the immediate context. Avoid word-for-word translation when the task asks for prediction or meaning from context.

1. Read or listen for the task purpose. 2. Notice contextual clues. 3. Select relevant language. 4. Check meaning and form. 5. Compare alternatives. 6. Apply the choice. 7. Reflect on feedback.

Example: In a space mission task, identify the clue first and then use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing.

Ignoring context, translating every word, choosing an option because of one familiar word, overlooking audience and purpose, and failing to check the final response are common mistakes.

Can I use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing? Can I explain which clue supports my choice? Can I communicate the result clearly in English?

Outcome ENG.7.8.W5 develops the ability to use grammar and mechanics accurately in writing through space, technology, future plans and imagination.
